voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Thebes, Egypt, around five hundred twenty-five B.C. Herodotus writes that a Persian king sent fifty thousand men toward Siwa.
They never arrived, he says. And never came back.
He heard it from the oasis. As the men ate, a great south wind rose, and buried them in sand.
His is the only account. A claimed find, in two thousand nine, was never confirmed.
One Egyptologist argues there was no storm. Only a defeat, and a story to cover it. No trace has ever been confirmed.
